paragraphs: Kulicke and Soffa Industries, Inc. ("K&S," "we," "us," "our," or the "Company") is a global leader in semiconductor assembly technology, advancing device performance across automotive, compute, industrial, memory and communications markets. Founded on innovation in 1951, K&S is uniquely positioned to overcome increasingly dynamic process challenges – creating and delivering long-term value by aligning technology with opportunity.

We design, develop, manufacture and sell capital equipment and consumables and provide services used to assemble semiconductor devices, such as integrated circuits, power discretes, light-emitting diode ("LEDs"), and sensors. We also service, maintain, repair and upgrade our equipment and sell consumable aftermarket solutions and services for our and our peer companies' equipment. Our customers primarily consist of integrated device manufacturers ("IDMs"), outsourced semiconductor assembly and test providers ("OSATs"), foundry service providers, and other electronics manufacturers and automotive electronics suppliers.

Our goal is to be the technology leader and the most competitive supplier in terms of performance, cost and quality in each of our major product lines. Accordingly, we invest in research and engineering projects intended to expand our market access and enhance our leadership position in semiconductor assembly. We also remain focused on enhancing our value to customers through higher productivity systems, more autonomous capabilities and continuous improvement and optimization of our operational costs. Delivering new levels of value to our customers is a critically important goal.

K&S was incorporated in Pennsylvania in 1956. Our principal offices are located at 23A Serangoon North Avenue 5, #01-01, Singapore 554369 and 1005 Virginia Dr., Fort Washington, PA 19034, and our telephone number in the United States is (215) 784-6000. We maintain a website with the address www.kns.com. We are not including the information contained on our website as a part of, or incorporating it by reference into, this filing. We make available free of charge (other than an investor's own Internet access charges) on or through our website our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and any amendments to these reports, as soon as reasonably practicable after the material is electronically filed with or otherwise furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). Our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and amendments to those reports are also available on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov.
Our year end for fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023 was October 4, 2025, September 28, 2024, and September 30, 2023, respectively.

On October 7, 2023, an escalated armed conflict between Israel and the Hamas terrorist organization commenced, leading to a series of extended hostilities along Israel's border with the Gaza Strip. Though a further ceasefire between Israel and the Hamas terrorist organization took effect on October 10, 2025, there have been subsequent claims of breaches on both sides.

The Company has a manufacturing facility and a business office in Haifa, and our capillaries are manufactured at our facilities in Israel and China. As of the date of this report, our business and manufacturing operations in Israel have not been impacted and no material damage or utilities interruptions have been noted at our Israeli facility. Trade routes remain open, and our suppliers and business partners in Israel remain operational. Furthermore, disruption to our workforce has been minimal.
Given that any further escalation or other hostilities cannot be excluded, we continue to monitor the situation and remain ready to activate our Business Continuity Plan ("BCP") if necessary.

On March 25, 2025, the Board of Directors the Company approved a strategic plan related to the cessation of the Company's EA equipment business. As part of the plan, the Company began the process of winding down the EA equipment business in an effort to prioritize core semiconductor assembly business opportunities and enhance overall through-cycle financial performance. The cessation of the EA equipment business is subject to a consultation process with the applicable works council and union representatives, which the Company initiated in the third fiscal quarter of 2025 and, as of October 4, 2025, had substantially completed. The wind down activities remains ongoing and are expected to be substantially completed by fiscal 2026, after which there will be some service support activities to serve out the remaining customer obligations. For additional information, see "Note 17: Cessation of Business" in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements in "Part II, Item 8 — Financial Statements and Supplementary Data".

The Company was engaged by one of its customers (the "Customer") to support the Customer with the development and future mass production of certain technologies relating to advanced display (the "Project"), previously referred to as Project W. As previously disclosed in fiscal 2024, in connection with the Customer's strategic review of its business, the Customer informed the Company that it cancelled the Project.

On November 4, 2024, the Company and the Customer entered into a written agreement pursuant to which the Customer agreed to reimburse the Company for certain costs and expenses that the Company incurred in connection with the Project. Pursuant to the agreement, the Customer agreed to pay $86.2 million to the Company. In the quarter ended December 28, 2024, $15.1 million was included within "Net Revenue" for delivered products and the remaining $71.1 million was included in "Gain relating to cessation of business" in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. In the quarter ended March 29, 2025, the Company received the reimbursement amount from the Customer.

The cost of logistics remains high as a result of macroeconomic conditions, inflation and labor shortages across layers of the supply chain. The Company's management continues to monitor for signs of any expansion of economic or supply chain disruptions or broader supply chain inflationary and logistical costs resulting either directly or indirectly from the tensions in the Middle East or between Ukraine and Russia, as well as the imposition of new, increased or retaliatory tariffs.

The ongoing tensions in the Middle East, including the Israel-Iran war, and the prolonged Ukraine/Russia conflict have not had a material impact on our financial condition and operating results in fiscal 2025. We believe that our existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, and anticipated cash flows from operations will be sufficient to meet our liquidity and capital requirements, notwithstanding the ongoing tensions in the Middle East and the prolonged Ukraine/Russia conflict and other macroeconomic factors, for at least the next twelve months from the date of this Annual Report. However, this is a highly dynamic situation. As the macroeconomic situation remains highly volatile and the geopolitical situation remains uncertain, there is uncertainty surrounding the operations of our manufacturing locations, our business, our expectations regarding future demand or supply conditions, our near- and long-term liquidity and our financial condition. Consequentially, our operating results could deteriorate.

The current macroeconomic conditions and declining consumer sentiment during fiscal years 2023 and 2024 have persisted, which continues to exacerbate inventory buildup in the semiconductor industry. Many of our customers who accumulated our products in the past three years continue to reduce their order rates as a result of inventory adjustment.

headings: Our operating results and financial condition could be adversely impacted by volatile worldwide economic conditions and unpredictable spending by our customers due to uncertainties in the macroeconomic environment.
International political instability, geopolitical tensions, terrorist acts and acts of war may adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.
The semiconductor industry is volatile with sharp periodic downturns and slowdowns. Cyclical industry downturns are made worse by volatile global economic conditions.
Difficulties in forecasting demand for our product lines may lead to periodic inventory shortages or excesses.
Our quarterly operating results fluctuate significantly and may continue to do so in the future.
Our average selling prices usually decline over time and may continue to do so.
We may not be able to rapidly develop, manufacture and gain market acceptance of new and enhanced products required to maintain or expand our business.
We may be unable to continue to compete successfully in the highly competitive semiconductor equipment and packaging materials industries.
Catastrophic events, such as pandemics and extreme weather events as a result of climate change, can have a material adverse effect on our operations and financial results.
We are subject to export restrictions that may limit our ability to sell to certain customers, and trade wars, in particular the U.S.-China trade war, could adversely affect our business.
Because a small number of customers account for most of our sales, our net revenue could decline if we lose a significant customer.
We maintain a backlog of customer orders that is subject to cancellation, reduction or delay in delivery schedules, which may result in lower than expected revenues.
The cessation of our Electronics Assembly equipment business may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Our business depends on attracting and retaining management, sales and technical employees as well as on the succession of senior management.
Alternative packaging technologies may render some of our products obsolete and materially and adversely affect our overall business and financial results.
Undetected problems in our products could directly impair our financial results.
We may not be able to continue to consolidate or relocate manufacturing and other facilities or entities without incurring unanticipated costs and disruptions to our business.
We may be materially and adversely affected by environmental and safety laws and regulations, including laws and regulations implemented in response to climate change.
We may acquire or divest businesses or enter into joint ventures or strategic alliances, which may materially affect our business, financial condition and operating results.
Increasing attention to ESG matters, including any targets or other ESG initiatives, could result in additional costs or risks or adversely impact our business
Our success depends in part on our intellectual property, which we may be unable to protect.

Third parties may claim we are infringing on their intellectual property, which could cause us to incur significant litigation costs or other expenses, or prevent us from selling some of our products.
Information Technology and Enterprise System Risks
We may be subject to disruptions or failures in our information technology systems and network infrastructures that could have a material adverse effect on us.
paragraphs: Though the semiconductor industry's cycle can be independent of the general economy, global economic conditions may have a direct impact on demand for semiconductor units and ultimately demand for semiconductor capital equipment and tools. Accordingly, our business and financial performance is impacted, both positively and negatively, by fluctuations in the macroeconomic environment. Expenditures by our customers depend on the current and anticipated market demand for semiconductors and products that use semiconductors, LEDs and batteries, including mobile devices, personal computers, consumer electronics, telecommunications equipment, automotive components, electric vehicles and other industrial products. Reductions or other fluctuations in our customers' spending as a result of uncertain conditions and volatility in the macroeconomic environment, including from government, economic or fiscal instability, economic recession, actual or potential inflation, rising interest rates, slower growth in certain geographic regions, global trade issues, global health crises and pandemics, restricted global credit conditions, reduced demand, excess inventory, higher energy prices, or other conditions, could adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results. Further, our profitability can be affected by volatility because we incur a certain amount of fixed costs that we cannot modulate up and down to meet increases or decreases in demand. The impact of broad-based weakening in the global macroeconomic environment could make our customers cautious and delay orders until the economic outlook becomes clearer. Significant downturns in the market for semiconductor devices or in general economic conditions reduce demand for our products and can materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results. Our visibility into future demand is generally limited and forecasting is difficult, and we believe historic, industry-wide volatility will persist.

The threat of terrorism or acts of war, risks and rumors of war, escalation and civil disturbances, including the prolonged tensions in the Middle East and the Ukraine/Russia conflict, increases the uncertainty in our markets and could adversely affect our business. On October 7, 2023, an escalated armed conflict between Israel and the Hamas terrorist organization commenced, leading to a series of extended hostilities along Israel's border with the Gaza Strip. Though a ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, there have been subsequent claims of breaches on both sides.

Many multinational companies in the semiconductor industry have research, design and development centers situated in Israel. The Company has a manufacturing facility and a business office in Haifa, and our capillaries are manufactured at this facility, in addition to our facility in China.

The intensity, duration and outcome of the ongoing war is uncertain and its continuation or escalation may have a material adverse effect on our business and operations. While we are currently maintaining business and operations in Israel without material damage or interruptions at our Israeli facility, our assets and operations in Israel could be vulnerable to future property damage, inventory loss, business disruption, and expropriation.

As the intensity of the war has been rapidly evolving, including the potential for heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, we continue to review reports concerning our operations and business partners and remain vigilant. Where necessary, we will ramp up our manufacturing capabilities in China as part of our general business contingency strategy.

The risk of cybersecurity incidents may also increase in connection with the ongoing war. These attacks may impact critical infrastructure and financial institutions globally, which in turn could adversely affect our operations. While we have taken actions to mitigate such potential risks, the proliferation of malware from the war into systems unrelated to the war, or cyberattacks targeted against U.S. companies, could adversely affect our operations.

paragraphs: This section of this Form 10-K generally discusses fiscal 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between fiscal 2025 and 2024. Discussions of fiscal 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between fiscal 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of the 2024 Annual Report filed on November 16, 2024 (the "2024 Annual Report").

Our Management's Discussion and Analysis ("MD&A") is provided in addition to the accompanying consolidated financial statements and notes to assist readers in understanding our results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows. The MD&A is organized as follows:
•Overview: Introduction of our operations, key events, business environment, technology leadership, products and services
•Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates •Recent Accounting Pronouncements •Results of Operations
•Liquidity and Capital Resources •Other Obligations and Contingent Payments Overview
For an overview of our business, please see "Part I, Item 1 — Business".

The preparation of consolidated financial statements requires us to make assumptions, estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, net revenue and expenses during the reporting periods, and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities as of the date of the consolidated financial statements. On an ongoing basis, we evaluate estimates, including, but not limited to, those related to accounts receivable, reserves for excess and obsolete inventory, carrying value and lives of fixed assets, goodwill and intangible assets, income taxes, equity-based compensation expense and warranties. We base our estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions that we believe to be reasonable. As a result, we make judgments regarding the carrying values of our assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources. Authoritative pronouncements, historical experience and assumptions are used as the basis for making estimates, and on an ongoing basis, we evaluate these estimates. Actual results may differ from these estimates.

We believe the following critical accounting policies, which have been reviewed with the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors, reflect our more significant judgments and estimates used in the preparation of our consolidated financial statements.

In accordance with ASC No. 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers, the Company recognizes revenue when we satisfy performance obligations as evidenced by the transfer of control of our products or services to customers. In general, the Company generates revenue from product sales, either directly to customers or to distributors. In determining whether a contract exists, we evaluate the terms of the agreement, the relationship with the customer or distributor and their ability to pay.

The Company recognizes revenue from sales of our products, including sales to our distributors, at a point in time, generally upon shipment or delivery to the customer or distributor, depending upon the terms of the sales order. Control is considered transferred when title and risk of loss pass, when the customer becomes obligated to pay and, where applicable, when the customer has accepted the products or upon expiration of the acceptance period. For sales to distributors, payment is due on our standard commercial terms and is not contingent upon resale of the products.
Our business is subject to contingencies related to customer orders, including:

•Right of Return: A large portion of our revenue comes from the sale of equipment used in the semiconductor assembly process. Other product sales relate to consumable products, which are sold in high-volume quantities, and are generally maintained at low stock levels at the customer's facility. Customer returns have historically represented a very small percentage of customer sales on an annual basis.

•Warranties: Our equipment is generally shipped with a one-year warranty against manufacturing defects. We establish reserves for estimated warranty expense when revenue for the related equipment is recognized. The reserve for estimated warranty expense is based upon historical experience and management's estimate of future expenses, including product parts replacement, freight charges and labor costs expected to be incurred to correct product failures during the warranty period.

•Conditions of Acceptance: Sales of our consumable products generally do not have customer acceptance terms. In certain cases, sales of our equipment have customer acceptance clauses which may require the equipment to perform in accordance with customer specifications or when installed at the customer's facility. In such cases, if the terms of acceptance are satisfied at our facility prior to shipment, the revenue for the equipment will be recognized upon shipment. If the terms of acceptance are satisfied at our customers' facilities, the revenue for the equipment will not be recognized until acceptance, which is typically obtained after installation and testing, is received from the customer.

paragraphs: Kulicke and Soffa Industries, Inc. ("K&S," "we," "us," "our," or the "Company") 為半導體封裝技術的全球領導者，於汽車、計算、工業、記憶體及通訊市場推進裝置性能。自1951年以創新為基礎成立以來，K&S 位於獨特位置，以應對日益動態的製程挑戰 – 透過將技術與機會結合，創造並交付長期價值。

我們設計、開發、製造與銷售資本設備與消耗品，並提供用於組裝半導體裝置的服務，例如積體電路、功率離散元件、發光二極體 ("LEDs"), 以及感測器。我們亦提供設備的維護、保養、修復與升級服務，並銷售我們與我們同業公司設備的消耗品後市場解決方案與服務。我們的客戶主要為整合元件製造商 ("IDMs"), 委外半導體封裝與測試服務提供者 ("OSATs"), 製造服務提供者，以及其他電子製造商與汽車電子供應商。
我們的目標為在每項主要產品線中成為技術領導者，並在性能、成本與品質方面成為最具競爭力的供應商。因此，我們投資於研究與工程專案，以拓展我們的市場接觸範圍，並強化我們在半導體封裝領域的領導地位。我們亦持續專注於透過提高生產力系統、更自動化的能力與持續改善與最佳化我們的營運成本，來提升對客戶的價值。為客戶提供新的價值層次是極其重要的目標。

K&S 於 1956 年在賓夕法尼亞州註冊成立。本公司主要辦公室位於新加坡 554369 聖淘沙北大道 23A 號 5 號樓 01-01 號，以及美國賓夕法尼亞州福爾特華盛頓 19034 號 1005 維吉尼亞大道，本公司美國電話號碼為 (215) 784-6000。本公司維護一個網站，網址為 www.kns.com。本公司不將網站上所載資訊視為本申報文件的一部分，也不將其透過參考方式納入本申報文件。本公司於網站上免費提供（除投資人自行支付的互聯網使用費外）年度報告（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）、現況報告（Form 8-K）及這些報告的更正文件，於這些資訊電子提交至證券交易委員會（"SEC"）或以其他方式提供後盡速提供。本公司年度報告（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）、現況報告（Form 8-K）及這些報告的更正文件，亦可在 SEC 網站 www.sec.gov 查閱。
我們財務年度2025、2024及2023的結算日分別為2025年10月4日、2024年9月28日及2023年9月30日。
2023年10月7日，以色列與哈瑪斯恐怖組織之間爆發升級的武裝衝突，導致沿以色列與加沙走廊邊界一連串延長的敵對行動。儘管以色列與哈瑪斯恐怖組織於2025年10月10日達成進一步停火協議，但雙方隨後均有聲稱違反協議。
本公司在海法設有製造廠與業務辦公室，我們的毛細管於以色列與中國的廠區製造。截至本報告日，我們在以色列的業務與製造運作未受影響，且未於以色列廠區觀察到重大損壞或電力中斷。貿易路線保持暢通，我們在以色列的供應商與業務夥伴持續運作。此外，我們員工的運作受到的幹擾極為有限。
考慮到任何進一步升級或其它敵對行動均無法排除，我們持續監測此情況，並在必要時準備啟動我們的業務持續性計畫 ("BCP")。

於 2025 年 3 月 25 日，本公司董事會批准一項戰略計畫，與本公司停止 EA 裝備業務有關。根據該計畫，本公司開始風化 EA 裝備業務的程序，以優先處理核心半導體封裝業務機會，並提升整體週期財務表現。停止 EA 裝備業務需與適用的工會及勞工代表進行諮詢程序，本公司於 2025 年第三會計季啟動此程序，截至 2025 年 10 月 4 日已 substantially 完成。風化活動持續進行中，預計於會計 2026 年 substantially 完成，之後將有部分服務支援活動以履行剩餘客戶義務。如需更多資訊，請參閱「附註 17：業務停止」於「第二部分，第 8 項 — 財務報表及補充資料」中的「合併財務報表附註」。
本公司被其客戶（稱為「客戶」）委託，協助該客戶進行某些與先進顯示技術（稱為「專案」）有關的開發及未來大規模生產，該專案先前稱為專案 W。如先前於會計 2024 年所披露，根據該客戶對其業務的戰略評估，該客戶已通知本公司取消該專案。

於 2024 年 11 月 4 日，本公司與該客戶簽訂書面協議，根據協議，該客戶同意償還本公司因該專案所產生的某些成本及費用。根據協議，該客戶同意支付 86.2 百萬美元予本公司。在 2024 年 12 月 28 日結訖的會計季， 15.1 百萬美元已包含於「淨營收」中，剩餘 71.1 百萬美元則包含於「業務停止相關獲利」中於合併營運損益表。在 2025 年 3 月 29 日結訖的會計季，本公司已收到該客戶的償還金額。
物流成本因總體經濟條件、通貨膨脹及供應鏈各層級的勞動力短缺而持續高企。本公司管理層持續監測是否有任何經濟或供應鏈中斷擴張的跡象，或因中東地區或烏克蘭與俄羅斯之間的緊張關係，或新、增加或報復性關稅所導致的更廣泛供應鏈通貨膨脹及物流成本。

中東地區持續的緊張局勢，包括以色列與伊朗戰爭，以及烏克蘭與俄羅斯衝突的延長，對本公司會計 2025 年的財務狀況及營運結果尚未造成重大影響。我們相信，本公司現有的現金、現金等價物、短期投資及預期來自營運的現金流，將足以應付 liquidity 及資本需求，不論中東地區持續的緊張局勢及烏克蘭與俄羅斯衝突及其他總體經濟因素，至少在本年度年報日期起的十二個月內。然而，這是一個高度動態的情況。由於總體經濟情況仍然高度波動，地緣政治情況仍然不確定，因此本公司製造據點的營運、本公司業務、對未來需求或供應條件的預期、近及長遠 liquidity 及財務狀況均存在不確定性。因此，本公司營運結果可能惡化。
目前總體經濟條件及會計 2023 年與 2024 年消費者情緒下降的情況持續存在，這使得半導體產業的存貨積壓情況持續惡化。許多在過去三年內累積本公司產品的客戶，因存貨調整而持續減少訂單率。

paragraphs: 本節內容為本 Form 10-K 一般討論財務年度 2025 與 2024 的項目，以及財務年度 2025 與 2024 年間的年對年比較。有關財務年度 2023 的項目及財務年度 2024 與 2023 年間的年對年比較，且未包含於本 Form 10-K 中的內容，可參閱 2024 年年報中「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」部分，該年報於 2024 年 11 月 16 日提交（稱為「2024 年年報」）。
本公司管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析（"MD&A"）除附屬財務報表及附註外，亦提供給讀者以協助瞭解本公司營運成果、財務狀況及現金流。MD&A 的組織方式如下：
•總覽：介紹本公司營運、關鍵事件、營運環境、技術領導地位、產品與服務
•關鍵會計政策與會計估計 • 最近會計準則公告 • 營運成果
•流動性與資本資源 • 其他義務與或有付款總覽
如需瞭解本公司業務總覽，請參閱「第一部分，項目 1 — 業務」。

編製合併財務報表需要本公司做出假設、估計與判斷，這些會影響報告期間內資產與負債的金額、淨營收與費用，以及於合併財務報表日期之或有資產與負債之揭露。本公司持續評估這些估計，包括但不限於應收帳款、過多與陳舊存貨之備抵、固定資產之帳面價值與使用年限、商譽與無形資產、所得稅、基於權益之薪資費用與保固費用。本公司基於歷史經驗及其他我們認為合理的假設做出這些估計。因此，本公司對資產與負債之帳面價值做出判斷，這些判斷並非來自其他來源。權威性準則、歷史經驗與假設為做出估計的基礎，並持續評估這些估計。實際結果可能與這些估計不同。
本公司認為以下關鍵會計政策，已與董事會審計委員會審閱過，反映本公司在編製合併財務報表時所使用較為重要的判斷與估計。
依 ASC 號 606 規則「與客戶之合約所產生之收入」，本公司於滿足履行義務時確認收入，即本公司產品或服務之控制權已轉移至客戶為證據。通常，本公司之收入來自產品銷售，或直接銷售予客戶，或銷售予經銷商。在判斷合約是否存在時，我們評估協議條款、與客戶或經銷商之關係及其付款能力。
本公司於銷售產品時確認收入，包括銷售予經銷商，於特定時點確認，通常為出貨或交付予客戶或經銷商，視銷售訂單之條款而定。控制權被視為已轉移，為產品或服務之所有權與損失風險已轉移，為客戶成為付款義務人，且於適用時，為客戶已接受產品或接受期屆滿。對於銷售予經銷商，付款為本公司標準商業條款，且不依賴產品之再銷售。
本公司業務受客戶訂單相關事項之影響，包括：
•退貨權利：本公司收入之大部分來自用於半導體封裝流程之設備銷售。其他產品銷售與消耗性產品有關，這些產品以高數量銷售，且通常於客戶廠區維持低存貨水平。客戶退貨歷來代表客戶銷售額之極小百分比。
•保固：本公司設備通常附有製造瑕疵之一年保固。於確認相關設備之收入時，本公司建立預估保固費用之備抵積累。預估保固費用之備抵積累基於歷史經驗及管理層對未來費用之預估，包括產品零件更換、運費及勞務成本，預計於保固期間內修正產品故障所產生之費用。
•接受條件：本公司消耗性產品之銷售通常不具客戶接受條款。在某些情況下，本公司設備之銷售可能包含客戶接受條款，可能要求設備依照客戶規格運作，或安裝於客戶廠區。在這種情況下，若接受條件於本公司廠區內於出貨前已達成，則設備之收入於出貨時確認。若接受條件於客戶廠區內達成，則設備之收入將於取得客戶之接受確認時確認，通常為安裝及測試後取得客戶之接受確認。

headings: 半導體產業與總體經濟風險
我們的營運成果與財務狀況可能因全球經濟條件的不穩定及客戶支出的不可預測性而受到負面影響，這是因為總體經濟環境的不確定性所致。
國際政治動盪、地緣政治緊張、恐怖攻擊及戰爭行為可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成負面影響。
半導體產業具有高度波動性，並會出現劇烈的週期性衰退與減速。週期性產業衰退會因全球經濟條件的波動而更加嚴重。
預測我們產品線的需求困難，可能導致週期性存貨不足或過多。
我們的季度營運成果有顯著波動，並可能在未來持續如此。
我們的平均銷售價格通常會隨時間下降，並可能持續如此。
我們可能無法迅速開發、製造並獲得新產品與升級產品的市場接受度，以維持或擴大我們的業務。
我們可能無法持續在高度競爭的半導體設備與包裝材料產業中成功競爭。
災難性事件，例如疫情與因氣候變遷所致的極端天氣事件，可能對我們的營運與財務結果造成重大不利影響。
我們受到出口限制的影響，可能限制我們對某些客戶的銷售能力，且貿易戰，特別是美國與中國的貿易戰，可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
由於少數客戶佔據我們銷售額的大多數，若我們失去重要客戶，我們的淨收入可能下降。
我們維持客戶訂單的積壓，但這些訂單可能被取消、減少或延遲交貨，這可能導致收入低於預期。
我們電子組裝設備業務的終止可能對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司業務依賴吸引及留住管理階層、銷售及技術人員，以及高階管理階層的繼任。
替代包裝技術可能使部分產品過時，並對本公司整體業務及財務結果造成重大且不利的影響。
產品中未被發現的問題可能直接影響本公司財務結果。
本公司可能無法在不產生預期外成本及營運中斷的情況下，持續進行製造及其他設施或機構的整合或遷移。
本公司可能因環境及安全法規，包括因應氣候變遷而實施的法規，而遭受重大且不利的影響。
本公司可能取得或出售業務或成立合資企業或戰略聯盟，此等行動可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大影響。
對環境、社會及治理（ESG）事項日益重視，包括任何目標或其他ESG倡議，可能會導致額外成本或風險，或對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司成功在部分程度上取決於智慧財產權，而本公司可能無法有效保護智慧財產權。
第三方可能聲稱本公司侵權其智慧財產權，此可能導致本公司產生重大訴訟費用或其他費用，或阻止本公司銷售部分產品。
資訊科技與企業系統風險
本公司可能面臨資訊科技系統及網路基礎設施中斷或故障，此可能對本公司產生重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 雖然半導體產業的週期可能獨立於總體經濟，但全球經濟狀況可能對半導體單元的需求產生直接影響，進而影響半導體資本設備和工具的需求。因此，我們的業務和財務表現會因總體經濟環境的波動而受到正負雙方面的影響。我們客戶的支出取決於目前及預期的半導體及使用半導體、LED 和電池的產品需求，包括行動裝置、個人電腦、消費電子產品、電信設備、汽車零組件、電動車及其他工業產品。由於不確定條件及總體經濟環境的波動，包括來自政府、經濟或財政不穩定、經濟衰退、實際或潛在的通貨膨脹、利率上升、某些地區成長放緩、全球貿易問題、全球健康危機和疫情、全球信貸條件受限、需求減少、能源價格上升或其他條件，導致我們客戶支出減少或出現其他波動，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。此外，我們的獲利能力可能因波動而受到影響，因為我們承擔了一定程度的固定成本，而無法根據需求的增加或減少而調整這些成本。全球總體經濟環境的廣泛弱化可能會使我們的客戶變得謹慎，並延後訂單，直到經濟前景變得更明確。半導體設備市場或總體經濟的重大衰退會減少對我們產品的需求，並可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。我們對未來需求的預測能力通常有限，預測困難，我們認為歷史性的產業-wide 波動將持續存在。

恐怖主義或戰爭的威脅、戰爭或戰爭 rumours 的風險、戰爭升級及民事動亂，包括中東地區的長期緊張局勢及烏克蘭/俄羅斯衝突，會增加我們市場的不確定性，並可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。2023 年 10 月 7 日，以色列與哈瑪斯恐怖組織之間的 escalated 武裝衝突開始，導致以色列與加沙地帶邊境一連串的長期衝突。儘管 2025 年 10 月 10 日已達成停火協議，但雙方隨後均有聲稱違反停火協議。
許多半導體產業的跨國公司均在以色列設有研究、設計及開發中心。本公司在海法設有製造廠與業務辦公室，我們的 capillaries 也在該廠製造，以及我們在中國的廠區。
持續戰爭的強度、持續時間及結果均不確定，其持續或升級可能對我們的業務及營運產生重大不利影響。儘管我們目前在以色列的廠區維持業務及營運，且未造成重大損失或中斷，但我們在以色列的資產及營運可能面臨未來財產損壞、存貨損失、業務中斷及沒收的風險。
隨著戰爭的強度迅速演變，包括中東地區可能出現的更高地緣政治緊張局勢，我們持續審視有關我們營運及業務夥伴的報告，並保持警覺。如有必要，我們將在中國提升製造能力，作為我們一般業務應變策略的一部分。
與持續戰爭相關的風險，可能增加網路安全事件的發生。這些攻擊可能影響全球關鍵基礎設施及金融機構，進而可能對我們的營運產生不利影響。儘管我們已採取行動以緩解這些潛在風險，但戰爭所衍生的惡意軟體擴散至與戰爭無關的系統，或針對美國公司的網路攻擊，可能對我們的營運產生不利影響。
